_comment: Tagalog function-word policy (tunatale-w4m7.4). 2026-10-14 (the user): the test is PICTUREABILITY, not part of speech. A root that can be pictured and extended with affixes is a vocab card, never a cloze; a cloze is for a word nothing can picture. So 'pos' is EMPTY and 'include' is the whole policy. The lemma table carries Wiktionary's UPOS, and that tags productive roots as closed-class: Cebuano gikan (from; mogikan 'depart', gigikanan 'origin') and uban (with; mouban) as ADP, duha (two) as DET; Tagalog mula and galing as ADP. A POS route would cloze them all. 'include' names the genuine difficulties for an English speaker, whatever UPOS the table gives them (several default to a rare NOUN homograph in Wiktionary, e.g. si, ba, nga): the case MARKERS ang/ng/sa, the personal-name markers si/ni/kay and their plurals, the plural 'mga', the inversion marker 'ay', 'nang' (the ng/nang choice is the most common written error), and the second-position particles ba/pa/na/din/rin/lang/naman/nga. 'po'/'opo' are NOT clozed: they are a register choice the style guide governs, and a blank that 'po' answers teaches nothing. 'clozes_only_verbs' is empty: Tagalog has no person/number conjugation (the biti case in sl.json). 2026-10-14: 'at' (and) and 'o' (or) added, the parallels of Cebuano 'ug' and 'o'; they had reached the cloze route only by their tag.
